'''Yuan Wang''' ({{lang-zh|王沅}}) is a Chinese-American mathematician specializing in [[control theory]] and known for her research on [[input-to-state stability]]. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Florida Atlantic University]], chair of the university's Department of Mathematical Sciences,{{r|chair}} and a moderator for the [[arXiv]] mathematical preprint repository in the areas of optimization and control (math.OC) and systems and control (cs.SY).{{r|fau}}

==Education and career==
Wang studied mathematics at [[Shandong University]] in China, graduating with a bachelor's degree in 1982.{{r|cv}} She completed a Ph.D. in 1990 at [[Rutgers University]], with the dissertation ''Algebraic Differential Equations and Nonlinear Control Systems'' supervised by [[Eduardo D. Sontag]].{{r|mg}}

She joined Florida Atlantic University as an assistant professor of mathematics in 1990. She was promoted to associate professor in 1995 and full professor in 2000.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Wang was named as an [[IEEE Fellow]] in 2013, "for contributions to stability and control of nonlinear systems".{{r|css}}
